code: if (requireNamespace("medfit", quietly = TRUE) &&     utils::packageVersion("medfit") >= "0.9.0") {   d <- as.data.frame(memory_exp)   d$x <- as.numeric(d$x) - 1   syntax <- paste("repetition ~ a1*x", "imagery ~ a2*x",                   "recall ~ cp*x + b1*repetition + b2*imagery", sep = "\n")   full <- medfit::fit_sem(syntax, d, fixed_x = FALSE, meanstructure = NULL)   null <- medfit::fit_sem(paste(syntax, "a1*b1 == 0", sep = "\n"), d,                           fixed_x = FALSE, meanstructure = NULL)   mbco(null, full) # statistic 0.0831, df 1 } if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{ data(memory_exp) memory_exp <- as.data.frame(memory_exp) # mxData() does not accept tibbles memory_exp$x <- as.numeric(memory_exp$x) - 1 # manually creating dummy codes endVar <- c("repetition", "imagery", "recall") # endogenous variables (not "x") manifests <- c("x", "repetition", "imagery", "recall") full_model <- OpenMx::mxModel(   "memory_example",   type = "RAM",   manifestVars = manifests,   OpenMx::mxPath(     from = "x",     to = endVar,     arrows = 1,     free = TRUE,     values = .2,     labels = c("a1", "a2", "cp")   ),   OpenMx::mxPath(     from = "repetition",     to = "recall",     arrows = 1,     free = TRUE,     values = .2,     labels = "b1"   ),   OpenMx::mxPath(     from = "imagery",     to = "recall",     arrows = 1,     free = TRUE,     values = .2,     labels = "b2"   ),   OpenMx::mxPath(     from = manifests,     arrows = 2,     free = TRUE,     values = .8   ),   OpenMx::mxPath(     from = "one",     to = manifests,     arrows = 1,     free = TRUE,     values = .1   ),   OpenMx::mxAlgebra(a1 * b1, name = "ind1"),   OpenMx::mxAlgebra(a2 * b2, name = "ind2"),   OpenMx::mxCI("ind1", type = "both"),   OpenMx::mxCI("ind2", type = "both"),   OpenMx::mxData(observed = memory_exp, type = "raw") ) ## H0: a1*b1 = 0 holds if a1 = 0 or b1 = 0. Fit one linear null per path and ## report the smaller statistic (what medfit::mbco_sem() automates). A single ## nonlinear null ind1 == 0 can converge to the wrong branch (rmediation#35). ## Build each h0 from the unfitted model: a constraint refit from the fitted ## model's estimates can stop at an infeasible point. null_a1 <- OpenMx::mxModel(   model = full_model,   name = "Null a1 = 0",   OpenMx::mxConstraint(a1 == 0, name = "a1_eq0_constr") ) null_b1 <- OpenMx::mxModel(   model = full_model,   name = "Null b1 = 0",   OpenMx::mxConstraint(b1 == 0, name = "b1_eq0_constr") ) full_model <- OpenMx::mxTryHard(full_model, checkHess = FALSE, silent = TRUE) null_a1 <- OpenMx::mxTryHard(null_a1, checkHess = FALSE, silent = TRUE) null_b1 <- OpenMx::mxTryHard(null_b1, checkHess = FALSE, silent = TRUE) res_a1 <- mbco(null_a1, full_model) res_b1 <- mbco(null_b1, full_model) res_a1 res_b1 ## Test of H0: a1*b1 = 0 (df = 1): the smaller of the two statistics min(res_a1@statistic, res_b1@statistic) ## The same test in one call: fixes each path at 0 in a copy of the fitted ## full model and returns the binding branch (here b1, statistic 0.0831) mbco_product_null(full_model, c("a1", "b1")) } # }

title: RMediation 1.4.0
text: Complete architectural redesign: S7 now computational core, legacy functions thin wrappers. Zero breaking changes: existing code continues work exactly (100% backward compatible). Enhanced extensibility: New computational architecture makes adding CI methods features straightforward.

title: RMediation 1.4.0
text: Introduced S7 object-oriented programming modern, type-safe class definitions. ProductNormal: Represents distribution product normal random variables. MBCOResult: Encapsulates results MBCO tests. New S7 Generics: cdf(), dist_quantile(), ci(), print(), summary(), show(). S7 classes include comprehensive display methods (print, summary, show) meaningful output.

title: RMediation 1.4.0
text: Breaking limitation removed: Can now compute confidence intervals products 3 variables. Works Monte Carlo method (type = "mc"). Example: ProductNormal(mu = c(0.3, 0.4, 0.5), Sigma = diag(3)) three-way products. Previous versions limited 2-variable products .

title: RMediation 1.4.0
text: New internal S7 functions: .compute_ci_dop(), .compute_ci_mc(), .compute_ci_asymp(), .compute_cdf_dop(), .compute_cdf_mc(), .compute_quantile_dop(), .compute_quantile_mc(). core algorithms now work ProductNormal objects natively. Legacy functions (medci(), pprodnormal(), qprodnormal()) convert parameters dispatch S7 core. Identical numerical results previous versions (validated 201 tests).

title: RMediation 1.4.0
text: numeric: Legacy support direct coefficient/covariance input. lavaan: Automatic extraction CI computation indirect effects. ProductNormal: Native S7 class support. Auto-detection: Automatically identifies product parameters (e.g., ab := *b) lavaan models. Renamed first argument mu better legacy compatibility.

title: RMediation 1.4.0
